title: Alpenglow Transit — Onboarding Acceptance Dossier & Prompt Set
summary: Acceptance dossier for Alpenglow Transit model onboarding. Contains pinned prompts (system + customer-facing), private dataset references and access notes, explicit acceptance criteria with numeric thresholds, prioritized regression scenarios, quick-run test checklist for release candidate, and sign-off record. This doc is intentionally pragmatic: checklist items, known open risks, and minimal reproducible test inputs for partner QA.
body:
Context:
Alpenglow Transit (customer) is integrating conversational routing and schedule QA into their driver dispatch console and rider support chat. They require on-prem/private deployment with strict PII controls and a low-tolerance for hallucinations. This dossier bundles the eval artifacts we will use to gate the model for Dedicated/Private deployment.

Notes to reviewers:
- Focus first on hallucination and extraction fidelity for stop IDs and time windows.
- We assume RBAC + KMS for dataset access; see private_datasets for S3 paths.
- Performance SLOs are strict: p95 inference latency <= 120ms on dedicated T4 pools for short prompts; higher-latency fallbacks must be documented.
- Unresolved: operational rollout plan for transitive timezone DST changes (ticket JIRA-ALPENGLOW-145).

Quick-run checklist (how to smoke-test a release candidate locally):
1) Pull model variant: redwood/alpenglow-v1.3-quant.
2) Run the 200-sample intent and extraction suite with the pairing dataset (see private dataset id).
3) Run the adversarial prompts (regression_scenarios) and ensure no hallucination >3%.
4) Measure token cost and latency; attach perf trace to PR.
5) Run privacy scrubber audit on outputs (automated script) and confirm no PII leakage in 500 sampled responses.

Known risks and mitigations:
- Ambiguous stop names across cities => we enforce canonical stop-id extraction and fallback to clarifying questions. Add a disambiguation step in the prompt template.
- Multi-lingual support (Spanish) has limited labeled data; we are using synthetic translation augmentation and will add targeted evals if recall drops.

Contact and escalation:
- Primary: Maya Chen (applied-ml)
pinned_prompts: SYSTEM: You are Alpenglow Assist, a strict information-extraction and routing assistant. Always prefer factual extraction. If the user request is missing key routing identifiers (stop_id, route, time window), ask a single clarifying question. Do NOT hallucinate stop names or addresses. Output must be JSON with fields: intent, slots, clarifying_question (nullable), confidence_score.

USER_PROMPT_TEMPLATE: 'I need help with [issue]. My trip is on [date] at [time]. Stop: [stop_name_or_id if known].' --- After the user text insert: 'Return JSON. If multiple plausible stops, include up to 3 candidates with canonical stop_id and confidence.'
SHORT: For short conversational snippets (<40 tokens) use the low-latency parser mode; do not attempt multi-step calendar normalization. Return normalized_time in ISO-8601 or null.

ESCALATION: If intent=driver_incident and severity keyword present (injury, accident, fire), set route_to='human-ops' and include incident_summary. Mark these responses with high confidence threshold 0.85 before automated routing.
private_datasets: vault://datasets/alpenglow/driver-incident-reports-2024 (access via secops sudo; contains redacted PII)
acceptance_criteria: Intent classification micro-F1 >= 0.92 across the 200-sample benchmark (weighted by class frequency) applied to ticketing-logs test split.
Slot extraction overall F1 >= 0.88 for stop_id, route_number, and time_window; per-slot floor stop_id >= 0.85.
Hallucination rate (asserted facts not present in input or canonical mapping) <= 3% on 500-sample adversarial set.
P95 inference latency <= 120ms on dedicated T4 profile using batch_size=1 low-latency pipeline for short prompts.
PII leakage score (automated scrub check) = 0 for redaction-sensitive fields on a 500-sample audit.
Regression: No more than 2% absolute erosion on core user flows compared to baseline model v1.1 on the regression slate.
Cost: average token cost per request under production mix <= $0.017 per request for the routed flow (measured on sample traffic).
regression_scenarios: DST-change queries: user mentions 'daylight saving' or ambiguous dates around Nov/Mar. Ensure normalization to correct local offset.
Partial stop data: truncated stop names (e.g., '5th & Ma'), driver shorthand ("brdge"), and misspellings. Must map to canonical stop_id or ask for clarification.
Adversarial hallucination tests: prompts that ask for non-existent stops or fabricated schedule changes; assistant must respond 'no record' rather than inventing times.
Multi-intent chaining: user asks to 'report incident and reroute bus 42' — system must extract two intents and prefer escalation path for incident before routing changes.
Spanish snippets: mixed-language user messages; intent accuracy check for Spanish subset (50 samples) must not drop more than 4% relative to English baseline.
